title: 60: LFH Internals
desc: Goal: Understand the Low Fragmentation Heap (LFH). The LFH activates after 18+ allocations of the same size class. Once active, it pre-allocates a UserBlocks region divided into fixed-size slots, and randomizes which slot is returned. This reduces fragmentation and adds exploit difficulty through unpredictable allocation order.
source: // is now active for this bucket.

logs.msg: The LFH is the front-end allocator for the NT Heap. It groups allocation sizes into 128 buckets (size classes). Bucket selection: sizes 1-256 use 8-byte granularity (bucket = ceil(size/8)), sizes 257-16384 use wider granularity. The LFH is NOT active by default -- it activates per-bucket after enough allocations of the same size.

HeapAlloc(h, 0, 32) -- alloc #1. The back-end handles this (LFH not yet active). Internally, _HEAP.FrontEndHeapUsageData[] counts how many times each bucket is hit. This counter increments with each HeapAlloc call for this size class.
HeapAlloc(h, 0, 32) -- alloc #2. Still served by the back-end. Each allocation for bucket 4 (size 32) increments the usage counter.
HeapAlloc(h, 0, 32) -- alloc #3. The counter is still below 18. All these are back-end allocations from the FreeLists or segment commit.
HeapAlloc × 13 more -- allocs #4 through #16 all served by the back-end. The usage counter climbs: 4... 8... 12... 16. Almost at the activation threshold.
HeapAlloc(h, 0, 32) -- alloc #17. The usage counter is nearing the activation threshold (18). Still served by the back-end. One more allocation of this size will trigger LFH activation for bucket 4.

HeapAlloc(h, 0, 32) -- alloc #18! The usage counter hits the activation threshold. LFH activates and this allocation is now served by LFH! The LFH allocates a UserBlocks region: a contiguous memory block subdivided into fixed-size slots. Each slot is exactly (header + 32) bytes. The LFH picks a slot using a randomized bitmap scan, not FIFO.

UserBlocks structure: _HEAP_USERDATA_HEADER at the start, followed by N fixed-size subsegment entries. A bitmap tracks which slots are busy/free. The LFH randomizes the starting position in the bitmap scan, so consecutive HeapAlloc calls do NOT return sequential addresses.

LFH randomization was added in Windows 8 to make heap spraying harder. Before Win8, LFH returned slots in a deterministic pattern. The randomization means an attacker spraying 1000 objects cannot predict which slot index will be adjacent to a target -- but statistical attacks still work with enough spray.

LFH activation demonstrated with all 18 allocations. Key facts: (1) LFH activates per-bucket after 18+ allocs of the same size. (2) Allocates from a UserBlocks region of fixed-size slots. (3) Uses bitmap-based tracking with randomized slot selection (Win8+). (4) Reduces fragmentation and raises the bar for heap manipulation attacks.

winMsg: You understand how the Low Fragmentation Heap activates, how UserBlocks subdivide memory into fixed-size slots, and how bitmap randomization affects exploitation.
